title: Price Responses of Rwandan Tungsten Exports under Conflict Minerals Regulation ---Period-by-Period Estimation of Export Demand Elasticity---
hypothesis: Export demand price elasticity of Rwandan tungsten varies across institutional/market regimes (pre-regulation, Dodd-Frank implementation, post-SEC enforcement change, post-2019 destination shift).
data_sources: UN Comtrade importer-reported trade for Rwanda HS 261100 (tungsten ores and concentrates) and global import data HS 261100 for world average price
sample: Monthly mirror trade panel of Rwandan tungsten ores and concentrates (HS 261100) by importing country, with importer-reported export values as dependent variable; quantity missing for some observations so unit values not continuously observed. World average price PtW merged plus exchange rate Ej t. Estimations by period with importer fixed effects and clustered SE at importer level.
method: 1. Construct monthly panel Jan 2009-Dec 2023: use importer-reported values X_jt for Rwanda HS261100 from UN Comtrade; exchange rates E_jt = importing-country currency per Rwandan franc from FXTOP monthly; world average price PtW = sum_i V_it / sum_i Q_it from global import data HS261100 each month (quantity-weighted).

2. Divide sample into four periods exactly as printed: Period 1 Jan. 2009--Dec. 2012 (48 months) pre-implementation baseline; Period 2 Jan. 2013--Apr. 2017 Dodd-Frank implementation; Period 3 May 2017--May 2019 after SEC April 2017 enforcement-policy change; Period 4 Jun. 2019--Dec. 2023 shift in export destinations observed in trade data.

3. Under small-country price-taker assumption, specify per-period fixed-effects reduced form: ln X_jt = mu_j + beta ln E_jt + gamma ln PtW_t + epsilon_jt, mu_j importer fixed effect; estimate by FE OLS separately by period with SE clustered at importing-country level.

4. Recover export demand elasticity via eta = beta - 1 under approximation omega=0, where omega is inverse-supply coefficient from ln UV_jt = a_j + omega ln X_jt + lambda ln PtW_t + e_jt estimated on subset with quantity observed. Report eta = beta-1 and 95% CI derived from beta SE.
5. Assess omega=0 approximation by estimating omega on quantity-observed subsample with importer FE and clustered SE; if p>0.05 and point estimate small, set omega=0 for eta calculation.

6. Test coefficient differences: for each pair (Period2-Period1, Period3-Period1, Period4-Period1, Period4-Period3) pool the two periods, estimate FE model allowing period-specific beta and gamma with importer x period FE, clustered SE at importer level, compute Delta beta = beta_s - beta_r, SE(Delta)=sqrt(Var_s+Var_r-2Cov), t=(beta_s-beta_r)/SE(Delta), p-value; Delta beta equals Delta eta under omega ~=0.
